task: Integrate the supplied gramophone violinist SVG character and its three motions into the existing game.

context.character: The Little Virtuoso: a living paper-craft wooden gramophone carrying a violin in its anatomical left hand and a bow in its right. The flower-shaped brass horn conveys emotion through tilts and follow-through.
context.user_intent: Enter walking with the instrument carried at his side, raise it into playing position, perform either one short note or a longer classical-style phrase with alternating bow strokes.
context.deliverable_type: Editable vector assets plus deterministic browser animation. The included motions are silent. Audio synchronization can be added only where the existing game provides audio.

before_editing: Read applicable AGENTS.md and existing project instructions. Inspect the current character markup, animation modules and actual game event flow.
Open index.html and inspect the reference motions and rig-manifest.json. When an image viewer cannot open SVG, render the SVG to PNG; inspect the XML directly for its groups and transforms.
Reuse the current frontend structure and build pipeline. For Razor Pages keep reusable character markup in the appropriate partial and initialization in the existing client module.
Identify the real events for character entrance, short feedback and longer performance. Do not invent backend APIs or map a generic event to a new game rule.

preserve: Recognizable cabinet silhouette, turntable, treble-clef emblem and flower horn
Visible wood facets, paper folds and joint discs
Violin outline, four strings, bridge, f-holes, chinrest and scroll
Thin bow with a distinct stick and hair
composition: Keep violin readable across the cabinet in the ready pose.
Keep both wrists visible around the neck and bow frog.
The bow can overlap the violin but must remain visually separate.
Use an appropriate stage viewport and safe margins so the horn, bow tip and feet are not accidentally clipped.
Use horn inclination, settling and restrained sway for personality. Avoid oversized squash/stretch on rigid wooden parts.

coordinate_rules.assetPlacement: Inline art groups preserve native coordinates; do not size every asset to the master viewBox. External SVG images need the asset viewBox minimum and dimensions as x/y/width/height.

contact_constraints: Left wrist follows the transformed violin neck grip.
Right wrist follows transformed bow grip.
While playing, bow hair crosses the bridge at every frame.
Solve arm elbows using two-bone IK; never independently tween the hands and props.
All arm, hand and prop transforms live under torso-root.
important_asset_notes: The left/right names are anatomical: left is on the viewer’s right in the ready pose.
Upper arms and forearms use local +X coordinates from the parent joint. Upper arm length is 135 and forearm length is 140.
Thigh and shin segments use local +X coordinates, with lengths 114 and 112.
violin.svg has its bridge at local [0,0], neck toward +X and neck grip at [208,0]. Rotate and translate the whole prop, then derive the left hand from that transform.
bow.svg has hair at local y=10 and the grip at [143,10]. During playing, translate along the bow axis while keeping its hair line through the violin bridge.
left-fingers.svg contains finger-1, finger-2 and finger-3. Small finger lifts are cosmetic and must not move the entire grip.
body.svg and horn.svg retain the original artwork coordinate systems. Their viewBoxes do not begin at [0,0].
gramophone-ready.svg and gramophone-carrying.svg are self-contained posed assemblies. The individual files are editable vector parts, not independent animation engines.

The demo uses inline SVG groups and references. To manipulate internals in a game, embed the SVG inline instead of treating the entire character as an . Prefix IDs and all href/url references when multiple character instances appear on one page.

short.description: one compact bow stroke, a small recoil, return to ready

long.description: four broad alternating bow cycles, finger articulation and gentle phrasing; seamless pose loop

full.description: entrance + short note + 0.8s pause + long phrase

entrance.carry: Violin bridge [798,972], angle -88 degrees. The bow is held upright at the viewer-left side. Left wrist follows the neck, right wrist follows the bow grip.
entrance.ready: Violin bridge [551,735], angle -16 degrees; bow angle 74 degrees.
entrance.leg_motion: Use alternating stance and swing, small knee bends and foot lift. Root movement should match the stance speed as closely as the existing stage allows. Avoid visible skating.
entrance.secondary_motion: Small cabinet bob, delayed horn tilt, a gentle settle before raising the violin.

short.gesture: One compact bow gesture and release. The preview uses a compact stroke followed by a recovery to the ready pose.
short.bow_travel: Up to a nominal 38 units shaped by a smooth envelope.
short.finish: Return all relevant transforms to the shared ready pose.

long.gesture: Four alternating bow cycles with a two-second period; larger strokes through the middle of the phrase.
long.bow_travel: Nominal amplitude 76 units, with a phrase envelope.
long.secondary_motion: Gentle cabinet sway and horn follow-through, with small left finger lifts.
long.loop: Start and end at the same ready pose. The cyclic bow velocity matches across the loop. Use a short envelope if starting from a completely still pose requires a softer launch.
long.musical_limit: This is stylized performance motion. Finger and bow patterns are not a transcription of a specific piece.

integration.preferred_approach: Adapt the supplied dependency-free requestAnimationFrame rig to the project’s existing animation layer. Do not add a second ticker if the project already has a central animation clock.
trigger_behavior: Entrance runs once when the intended game section becomes visible.
If a play request arrives during entrance, queue or coalesce it until the ready pose.
A short request plays once and returns to ready.
Long performance may loop while the actual game state requests it; stop at the phrase boundary when practical.
Rapid repeated triggers must not create overlapping tickers.
Restore or dispose animations according to the actual page/component lifecycle.
ux: For decorative use set aria-hidden=true; for meaningful status provide concise text outside the SVG.
Respect prefers-reduced-motion with a static ready pose or minimal transition.
Keep the game’s current quiz flow, input behavior, scoring and data contracts intact.
Keep motion controls in a development preview; only expose controls in the game if they serve the player.
Pause when hidden and avoid unnecessary frame updates while idle.
rendering: Use SVG transform attributes on joint groups for deterministic pivots.
Use the two-bone IK solver for both arms so hands remain attached to the props.
All arms, hands, violin and bow share torso-root; legs stay in the locomotion frame to allow floor contact.
Do not animate left/right/top to drive character motion.
Do not apply CSS transform-origin to the entire character when a joint pivot is intended.
When replacing only one asset, retain its pivot and coordinate contract.

acceptance_criteria: All SVG files parse and use editable vector elements with no embedded raster images or external network dependencies.
The character is visible on first load in the ready pose.
Entrance visibly walks in with violin and bow, then raises them into a coherent playing pose.
Short and long clips are visibly different and can be triggered independently.
Bow hair intersects the bridge throughout playing; the bow hand remains on the grip and the violin hand stays on the neck.
No detached joints, arm overextension, clipped props, NaN transforms or duplicate IDs within an instance.
Long loop endpoints match within numeric tolerance.
Pause, resume, restart, timeline seeking and reduced-motion behavior work in the preview.
Verify desktop and narrow layout in an actual browser available to the project.
Do not claim audio synchronization or integration with the game unless it has actually been implemented and tested.
completion_report: List changed files and how the game triggers each clip.
State how it was tested, including browser visual review and remaining limitations.
Provide a runnable preview and explain how to tune durations without breaking contact constraints.
